competencyRepair.draftAnswer: In my Corporate Finance module I was asked to value LVMH using public data. I built a DCF and a trading-comparables model in Excel, pulled annual-report figures for LVMH and three luxury-sector peers, and tested revenue growth assumptions of three, five and seven per cent. What I found was that the valuation was highly sensitive to the growth rate — a two-percentage-point shift moved the output materially [confirm: by how much, approximately?]. I presented the sensitivity range and my reasoning to my four-person seminar team and flagged that the result depended heavily on margin assumptions. At Redcliffe Partners I applied a similar structured approach, screening 12 software companies against an acquisition brief and flagging four based on their recurring-revenue models. I've learned that being explicit about what drives your numbers — and what could break your conclusion — is as important as the model itself. [confirm: what view did your LVMH range imply about market price?]

cv.sourceText:
Amelia Chen
Email: amelia@example.com
EDUCATION
University of Bristol — BSc Economics, 2023–2026. Final year. Predicted 2:1. Modules: Corporate Finance, Financial Accounting, Econometrics.
EXPERIENCE
Redcliffe Partners — Corporate Finance Intern, July–August 2025
Researched 12 UK software companies for a prospective acquisition screen. Recorded business descriptions, revenue and EBITDA where publicly available in an Excel comparison table. Flagged 4 companies for further review because their recurring revenue models matched the screen brief. Presented the comparison table and selection reasons to an associate. No transaction completion or client outcome was confirmed.
Pho House — Part-time Team Member, September 2023–present
Worked 12 hours per week alongside full-time study; trained 3 new colleagues on ordering and till procedures. During one busy service, spotted a duplicate payment, informed the shift lead and helped process the correction.
PROJECTS
LVMH valuation — University Corporate Finance project, 2025
Built a DCF and trading-comparables valuation in Excel using public annual-report data. Compared LVMH with 3 luxury-sector peers. Tested revenue growth assumptions of 3%, 5% and 7% and presented valuation sensitivity to a 4-person seminar team. Identified dependence on growth and margin assumptions; did not make a live investment recommendation.
ACTIVITIES
Economics Society — Member, 2024–2026. Attended employer talks. No committee position.
SKILLS
Excel, financial analysis, financial modelling, valuation, research, presentation. Languages: English and conversational Mandarin.
